findings.title: Saved video group_id is not bound to frame-derived source groups before normal/RQ4 resampling
findings.impact: The frame-to-score binder validates member_group_ids but omits group_id. A producer error can split or merge source groups in saved score rows and create matching bootstrap artifacts. The oracle then recomputes uncertainty using that wrong dependence structure, potentially returns PASS_SELECTED_D_CORE while frames prescribe different bootstrap units. Closure resampling derives groups independently and is not affected by this omission.

independent_probe.input: Four natural videos, 32 frames; original g0 and g1 each contain one real and one fake video; scores and all membership fields preserved. Only in-memory score.group_id replaced by its video_uid.
independent_probe.result: _bind_frame_scores accepts 60 scalar checks; _RankOracle.groups changes from 2 source groups to 4 independent video groups. Wrong grouping admits class-missing draws that the true paired source grouping cannot produce.
independent_probe.probe_type: Private synthetic in-memory only; no source mutation and no real data read.

findings.required_fix: Derive and compare score.group_id from each aggregation group using the unchanged scoring_d._video_scores rule at line122: first group_id when part.group_id.nunique()==1, otherwise None. Correct grouping is already constrained to one source group per natural video; collision groups spanning multiple source groups must retain None. Add directed normal/RQ4 regression rejection without editing original producer modules.
findings.disposition: Open; root and author notified before report publication.
